claims.text: Wear performance in high-entropy-alloy protective coatings is governed by an in-situ, stress-driven dynamic phase transformation or localized work hardening.
The proposed microstructural response is activated when alloy composition is tuned near a critical transformation threshold.
Wear-induced microstructural evolution increases surface hardness.
The increased surface hardness reduces wear volume during sliding relative to a stable, homogeneous alloy.
The initial coatings are homogeneous, multi-principal-element high-entropy alloys without significant wear-induced microstructural changes.
Adjusting the concentration of elements that destabilize the homogeneous phase can bring the coating near its transformation threshold.
Sliding stress causes alloys near the transformation threshold to undergo a stress-induced microstructural change.
The stress-induced microstructural change increases local hardness.
Local hardening lowers the material-removal rate and therefore lowers wear volume.
Coatings tuned near the transformation threshold will show higher surface hardness than compositions far from the threshold.
Coatings tuned near the transformation threshold will show lower wear volume than compositions far from the threshold.
Baseline coatings with stable, homogeneous microstructures will not undergo stress-induced transformation under the same wear conditions.
The proposed mechanism should operate over controlled loads and sliding speeds representative of service conditions.
High-temperature oxidation or other externally induced mechanisms can overwhelm the proposed stress-induced transformation effect.
The magnitude of the transformation effect and the critical composition threshold may differ among alloy systems.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis permits either a phase transformation or localized work hardening, but the falsification rule can reject the hypothesis merely because no stress-induced phase or microstructural change is detected. Absence of a phase transformation would not by itself exclude the alternative localized-work-hardening branch.
